title: Migrating my game from Claude to Google AI Studio (this is not a paid content...) and how I came to embraced vibe-coding...
author: baodingball
selftext:
Hello everyone.  I guess I can consider myself as a "vibe-coder", now that I have published two games on [Itch.io](http://Itch.io), where all the codes were created by AI.  It was not suppose to go that way.  I thought I would use ChatGPT every time I stumble on my python coding.  I am a  novice programmer who dabbled in C++, python, HTML, HTML5, Contruct2, Vassal Engine, and all sort of stuff.  With the advent of AI, I thought I would unearth a project buried for decades.  A text-based, turn-based mmorpg, playable on an internet browser. Pretty lame, huh?  Anyways, as the game progressed, I kept finding myself copy-pasting, copy-pasting, and copy-pasting codes spewed by the AI. First it was ChatGPT, then moved to DeepSeek, then Grok, then finally Claude, which I found to be the best.  When Claude gave me an estimated completion time of 12 weeks, based based on my working phase and how fast I copy-paste codes that I no longer understand, I started looking for ways to be more efficient.  I thought I would install Claude Code on my laptop so I can have the codes auto-generated, but the think is, it does not work unless you have a paid subscription.  Claude and I have finished most of the back-end stuffs.  We have setup the database server on SupaBase (also free), and doing test on game rules implementation.  At this point, I decided to dip my toe on Google AI Studio (which, surprisingly is also free).  Can not really remember how I heard about it. Probably through my constant searches on how to make my work faster.  So, I linked my GitHub repo to Google Studio, attached my game rules documents, the detailed roadmap Claude has prepared for me when I was starting the project, gave my summary prompt, and in just a few minutes, seconds even, I had a front end landing page on my preview window.  Holy $\^$&\^%!!! I can not even remember asking Google AI to do that.  I asked Google AI Studio to add more features, a working map, transport system, intel-gathering, assassination-strike, inventory, game-mater console, dark-web, NPC generator, random contract generator, mission generator, everything.  I have added all these game features without touching a single line of code.  I finally gave in.  The reason I want to learn to code is because I want to make games.  But taking that path at this stage of time in my life, is long and arduous.  I will probably breathe my last breath without seeing my games materials.

If you want to check my game, here it is:  
[https://tag-game-three.vercel.app/](https://tag-game-three.vercel.app/)  
[https://baodingball.itch.io/tag](https://baodingball.itch.io/tag)

comments.author: Equal-Border-7793
comments.body: Yes, Claude and GPT are currently more suitable for designing 3D and 2D games. Text-based games are not difficult to design and can be designed using relatively common models; Gemini 3.8 Flash is also very fast.

replies.author: baodingball
replies.body: Nope, not working for Google and I am not saying Google AI Studio is the best.  What I am saying is that I am an old dinosaur recently discovering the wonders of AI.  Google AI Studio solved my copy-pasting bottleneck with Claude, to which I am not subscribed.  I tried ClaudeCode but does not work with free accounts.  But Google offer that feature for free.  I no longer have to type the codes manually nor copy-pasting them back and forth.  All I have to do is prompt what I want and google give it to me on a running app, more or less. Updating my GitHub repo is a easy as well, just 3 clicks

replies.author: enigmaticy
replies.body: Try opencode, there are free tiers as well deepseek v4.1 flash is pretty good and decent. There are also others but either expensive or not qualified as for coding. You will be thank to me. You can even bring your own api key its easy to use. Ask ai how to setup.

replies.author: SlightOfHand_
replies.body: Yeah no Gemini is dogshit at most things, but part of Google’s problem is they have no focus. They have one hundred AI projects of various levels of completeness and usefulness, several of which overlap one another in haphazard ways. I’m talking about Google AI Studio, which is a specific tool which is decent at mocking up frontend design/UI. When I need to do web design sometimes I’ll see what it comes up with and hand it back to Claude as an example of what I want.
